triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix match on filing_status enumerated only joint (1), married-filing-separately (2) and single (0), so head-of-household and surviving-spouse taxpayers got no threshold at all, leaving 26 USC 3101(b)(2)(C)'s catch-all ('in any other case, $200,000') unrepresented for those statuses.
triage.triage_notes: MIXED MODULE - read carefully before using as a benchmark item. The rest of the diff (module.proof_validation.required plus metadata.proof.atoms blocks on all six rules) is mechanical provenance; only the match arms are meaning-bearing. The fix adds '4 => additional_medicare_wage_tax_joint_threshold' and '3 => additional_medicare_wage_tax_other_threshold'. Branch 3 (head of household) at $200,000 matches the statute's clause (C), which I read through the pinned corpus release: '(A) in the case of a joint return, $250,000, (B) in the case of a married taxpayer (as defined in section 7703) filing a separate return, 1/2 of the dollar amount determined under subparagraph (A), and (C) in any other case, $200,000.' Branch 4 (surviving spouse) at $250,000 is itself unsupported by (C) - a qualifying surviving spouse does not file a joint return - and follow-up commit 1e0518cbf 'Repair generated section 3101(b)(2) filing status threshold (#311)' flips '4 => additional_medicare_wage_tax_joint_threshold' to '...other_threshold' and rewrites the module summary's filing-status convention. So this commit fixes one missing branch correctly and introduces a second defect that a later commit repairs; that later commit is the cleaner amount/scope instance. The companion test added here (surviving_spouse_uses_joint_threshold, filing_status 4 -> 250000) encodes the wrong expectation. Confidence held at 0.6: the diff and test show the missing-coverage defect but the commit message is generic and the PR body describes an unrelated module.
triage.verifier_justification: The diff does change encoded meaning, so it is a fidelity fix, not mechanical: beyond the proof-atom metadata it adds two arms to the `additional_medicare_wage_tax_threshold` match, which pre-fix enumerated only filing_status 1, 2 and 0, so head-of-household (3) and surviving-spouse (4) tax units fell out of the rule entirely even though the module's own summary claimed to cover head of household. But the defect is filing-status coverage of the derived rule, not a missing clause: 3101(b)(2)(C)'s catch-all and its $200,000 were already encoded (`additional_medicare_wage_tax_other_threshold` = '200000', applied to status 0), so nothing about the clause was unrepresented — the rule simply applied to the wrong population, which the kind list assigns to wrong_entity_or_scope. The first reader's rationale is also partly contradicted by the fix itself: it maps status 4 to the $250,000 joint threshold, not to the catch-all, and the pinned corpus text reads "(A) in the case of a joint return, $250,000 ... (C) in any other case, $200,000" with no surviving-spouse language, which is why the later commit 1e0518cbf re-repaired `4 => additional_medicare_wage_tax_other_threshold`.
triage.verifier_notes: Bundle path statutes/26/3101/b/2.yaml, module index 2; commit ee7f9bc09a, parent 86e2549dc7. Two meaning-bearing added lines: "+              4 => additional_medicare_wage_tax_joint_threshold" and "+              3 => additional_medicare_wage_tax_other_threshold"; everything else in the diff is `proof_validation: required` plus per-rule proof atoms (provenance/mechanical). Corroboration that the pre-fix state was wrong rather than an unclaimed enhancement: the pre-fix test file already contained `head_of_household_above_threshold` (filing_status 3, expecting threshold 200000) with no matching arm in the formula, and the module summary already listed "3 = head of household" and "$200,000 in any other case". Pinned release us-rulespec-2026-07-13 (corpus commit 612d20ca43, body sha 3fa3fc0b75) gives 3101(b)(2) as "(A) in the case of a joint return, $250,000, (B) ... ½ of the dollar amount determined under subparagraph (A), and (C) in any other case, $200,000." Caveat worth recording in the corpus: this same commit INTRODUCED a second fidelity defect — `4 => joint_threshold` ($250,000 for a surviving spouse) has no basis in (A), and commit 1e0518cbf ("Repair generated section 3101(b)(2) filing status threshold (#311)", 2026-05-28) reversed it to `other_threshold` and rewrote the summary convention to "1 = joint" / "4 = surviving spouse / qualifying widow(er)". If the taxonomy prefers to route all additive-coverage fixes to unrepresented_clause, keeping the original kind is defensible; my objection is that clause (C) itself was already represented and only the filing-status population was wrong. Commit message is generic ("Repair generated RuleSpec validation coverage") and the PR (#25, "Encode 26 USC 63(c) standard deduction") says nothing about 3101, so the diff and the later #311 repair are the only evidence.
